prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: No open or discoverable solution operates autonomous mobile health clinics at any scale, let alone 1,000,000; the Main KPI is not met. A peer-reviewed review describes autonomous mobile clinics as prototypes requiring level 4 driving (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9421545/, roadmap at https://www.arxiv.org/pdf/2204.04841); the projects found are concepts or prototypes (Texas A&M telehealth van, Renault U1st Vision, Toyota e-Palette mobile clinic demo, a Nuro patent). Staffed, driver-operated mobile clinics are mature but small in number: about 2,000 in the United States (https://equityhealthj.biomedcentral.com/track/pdf/10.1186/s12939-020-1135-7) and over 500 in Zhejiang, China, each with a doctor, nurse and driver (https://www.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202507/28/WS6886cddca310ad07b5d924a5.html). Honest limit: both autonomous driving and mobile clinics are established fields; the open gap is safe autonomous operation on rural roads with remote clinical oversight, and work that only redesigns a staffed mobile clinic is not new.
